title.narrative: CO-El Nino Induced Food Insecurity: CAT2

description.narrative:
1. Armed Conflict in Cabo Delgado The Province of Cabo Delgado, in Mozambique, is a critical center for humanitarian aid due to thearmed conflict triggered by Non-State Armed Groups (GANEs), since September 2017, which has already displaced more than 2.2 millionpeople and of these 1.7 people have urgent humanitarian needs and require life-saving and life-sustaining care and assistance, as well as protection. 2. Drought _ Induced by the El Ninõ Phenomenon According to the FEWS NET Famine Early Warning Systems Network, asof April 2024, 690,000 hectares of crops (15 percent of the total planted area), mainly in the southern and central parts of the country, have been damaged by El Niño conditions and by extreme weather phenomena, leading to below-average harvests. In addition to adifficult harvest season, in February 2024 corn prices increased by 12 percent, marking a 24 percent price increase over the year 2023. Food prices are therefore expected to remain high due to the outlook of another below-average harvest in 2024-2025. Currently, it is estimated that 3.3 million people are food insecure (IPC3+). Despite Mozambique having not yet launched an appeal, the country’s 2024 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan indicate that a total of 2,250,000 million people need humanitarian assistance and protection, with around 1.7M people conflict affected in need of urgent humanitarian assistance.
The objective of the response project is threefold: a) provide immediate food assistance; b) improve the hygiene conditions of families seriously affected by drought and conflict and c) mitigate protection risks.
The objective of this project is to contribute to improving access to food, hygiene conditions and providing protection services for target communities. With this project, Oxfam and its partners aim to reach a total of 600 people (women, men, boys and girls) affected by the Conflict and Drought Induced by the ElNinõ Phenomenon in Cabo Delgado, Montepuez District. Oxfam in Southern Africa will manage and implement this multi-sectoral project through the local partner (AMA).
Specific Objective: 600 people affected by food insecurity and related vulnerabilities in Montepuez District are able to access immediately food and WASH assistance and adequate support for the protection and recovery of their livelihoods by December 2024.
Food Security The markets work but there is a gradual increase in the prices of basic foods (especially corn). Oxfam and its partners are planning a market assessment to understand not only the status of food reserves, but also to obtain details of prices in the districts where Oxfam is implementing its food security initiatives. Although food kits were the option identified for a rapid response in the project area, other food assistance options/modalities will be explored. Additionally, to promote sustainability of results, the project will work in close collaboration with relevant stakeholders and coordinate closely with the Food Security cluster.
Output 1: Oxfam and its partner AMA's Food Security emergency response activities ensure adequate access to food for target families. Activities: Activity 1. Community mobilization for food distribution (dissemination of selection criteria, etc.): - Beneficiaries registration. - beneficiaries verification. - validation of list of beneficiaries. Activity 2. Food distribution to the families in the resettlement centers and or/host communities. Activity 3. Nutrition education promotion messages at distributions points. Activity 4. Post food distribution monitoring (PDM).
WASH With people constantly on the move and with low purchasing power, with access to hygiene products and utensils being a critical need, the project will improve the hygiene conditions of families, through the distribution of hygiene kits that combine/complement the food assistance. Hygiene education is ongoing, community-led and implemented through WASH committees and hygiene promotion volunteers. Additionally, to promote sustainability of results, the project will work in close collaboration with relevant stakeholders and coordinate closely with the WASH cluster.
Output 2: The hygiene conditions of the families covered improved due to the interventions of the Oxfam project and its partner AMA. Activities: - Distribution of hygiene materials. - PDM.
Protection The protection of internally displaced persons (IDPs) will essentially include awareness-raising sessions on mitigating protection risks and fundamentally supported by safe programming. Specific protection activities will be guided by emerging humanitarian needs and specific subgroups of beneficiaries.
Output 3: Ensure safe programming and mitigate protection risks in reducing the risk and vulnerabilities of the most vulnerable population groups in the community. Activities: - Community awareness on protection against sexual abuse and exploitation. - Participate in Protection Cluster meetings. - Train community members on community-based reporting and feedback mechanisms. - Train community leaders and activists on protection against sexual abuse and exploitation. - Establish protection focal points at community level to follow up on cases. - Promotion of hygiene messages during the distribution of hygiene kits. - Link VBG or VCMR to district referral paths. - Awareness raising and regular monitoring of protection and risks of sexual exploitation and abuse in resettlement centers and/or host communities. - Establishment of community-based reporting/complaints and feedback mechanisms.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
